The technology-use purposes listed are relating to the feeding experiences of others, assuring infant feeding practice, finding solutions to challenges in infant feeding, and logging infant feeding practice.
The source context says the chart comes from a paper published at CHI in 2021.
The strongest positive responses are especially visible for finding solutions to challenges in infant feeding, where breastfeeding parents have 37.7% agree and 45.90% strongly agree.
For bottle-feeding parents, the alt text reports no strongly disagree or disagree responses for relating to the feeding experiences of others, while 41.67% agree and 33.33% strongly agree.

For partners, the most explicitly positive reported response is also in social and reassurance-oriented uses, with 41.18% agreeing both for relating to others' experiences and for assuring infant feeding practice.

The logging category differs from the others because breastfeeding parents show 34.92% strongly disagree alongside 25.40% strongly agree, partners show 31.25% strongly disagree alongside 31.25% strongly agree, and bottle-feeding parents show 50% strongly agree.
The inclusion of partners indicates that infant feeding support is not limited to the feeding parent alone, and digital tools may also play a role in shared caregiving or family coordination.
